The Roles view: every Role of Server.ServerCapabilities.RoleSet with the accounts it is granted to, read via the identity mapping rules (Part 18 4.4.3). Admin-gated (WIN_REQUIRES_ADMIN), read-only. THEME-GATED, so reshell-theme rather than auto-view: MakeRolesGridPanel() returns nullptr under the legacy theme (the whole user_access panel family does), so RolesView::Init builds no widget, OpenedView::Init throws 'Can't create widget', and the view never opens. Tagged auto-view until 2026-08-02, which made every default-pipeline run fail this capture - the admin gate was NOT the cause, the session holds Configure. To publish it, the panel factory must first drop its legacy gate (the publish subset admits auto-* only). KNOWN FIXTURE GAP: Members renders 'None' for every Role. The RoleSet and its Roles browse correctly - the capture shows both - but the identity-rule rows the fixture projects under them do not come back from the client browse, so no membership reaches the view. The read path itself is unit-tested against FakeNodeService (role_membership_unittest.cpp); it is the offline fixture's rule projection that is unproven. Fix that before publishing this image. The manual prose for this surface is written (scada-docs client/workbench.md + en/ mirror, #administration); the image is NOT embedded yet because the published set must come from the WINDOWS pipeline - a macOS render differs by font alone and would commit as churn. Embed it on the next Windows regeneration, set published:true and add it to current_generator_owned_subset.

The users-admin RBAC inspector (right region of users-admin.html) for the fixture's Администратор. Rewritten 2026-08-01 onto the ROLE model: it lists the Roles the account holds and derives the permission breakdown from them through the same default role->permission map the server enforces with, replacing the coarse Administrator/Operator/Observer pill that read the retired AccessRights bitmask - a pill that would have kept asserting authority for an account whose Role had been revoked. Three states stay distinct: the Roles list, 'None' (holds no Role - real, and grants nothing), and 'No data' (the RoleSet could not be read, which also suppresses every permission row). KNOWN FIXTURE GAP: this capture shows 'None' because the fixture's identity rules do not reach the client browse (same gap as roles.png); against a real server the account's Roles appear here.

Custom table (the CusTable window, SheetModel) — the free-form spreadsheet: literal labels beside '=<formula>' cells bound to live values, with a coloured title and header band. Untagged until 2026-08-01, so the managed-image gate skipped it, and the render was a blank grid: a sheet's content lives in its saved window as SheetCell/Column items, which no fixture spec could express. The spec now carries `cells` and `column_widths` (see screenshot_data.json), and the capture is guarded by a filled-cell count — a sheet's row and column counts do not move when its content vanishes, so only counting cells that rendered text can see it go empty. Column headers (A/B/C) and row numbers are deliberately absent: sheet_view.cpp shows them only in edit mode. A live cell renders its item's display format (Температура shows 42.3; Активная мощность has no format and shows 125). That exposed a third bug: a formula cell cached the text it formatted when the sheet opened, and nothing notifies when an item's format arrives, so `--only sheet.png` rendered raw values where a full run rendered formatted ones — and a real sheet opened before its nodes loaded stayed unformatted for the life of the window. Formula cells now format on read (SheetCell::GetDisplayText), and the two renders agree. Populating this capture found a teardown crash: ~SheetCell erases itself from SheetModel::blinking_cells_, which was declared after `cells_` and so destroyed before them — closing a sheet holding one blinking cell segfaulted in std::set::erase, reachable by any user whose custom table binds a cell to a live value. Fixed by declaration order, with a regression test in sheet_model_unittest.cpp. It also found the alignment bug this capture now demonstrates: per-cell alignment was parsed, stored and offered in the context menu but never reached the screen, because GridCell carried no alignment and the grid adapter handed Qt the aui enum raw — so every aui::Grid in the client rendered left-aligned whatever its columns asked for. Fixed in grid_model_adapter.cpp + GridCell, with tests in grid_model_adapter_unittest.cpp; summary.png and client-retransmission.png changed with it. macOS render pending a Windows re-render; validation-only.

Objects explorer (the Struct window, ObjectTreeModel) — the operator's device/signal tree, collapsed to its top level. Untagged until 2026-08-01, so the managed-image gate skipped it and the on-disk render sat two UI generations stale: it still showed the retired items.bmp glyphs (yellow folders, blue variable icons) from before both the Lucide SVG migration and the deliberate removal of per-row icons from this tree (ObjectTreeModel::ObjectTreeNode::GetIcon returns kNoIcon — principles.md §5, state is a dot, never artwork). Only the root row keeps a glyph. macOS render pending a Windows re-render; validation-only.

Files view (FileSystemView) — the server's file store as a tree: directories typed FileDirectoryType, files typed FileType, expanded. Untagged until 2026-08-01, so the managed-image gate skipped it, and the fixture defined no file nodes at all — the view rendered its single root row, which no row count could catch (hence min_columns' sibling fix: the tree row check now counts materialized descendants, not just top-level rows, and runs after the expand step). The fixture's file store is described under `_filesystem_comment` in screenshot_data.json; it also needed FileDirectoryType added to the shared ScadaTestAddressSpace and FileType corrected there from ObjectType to VariableType, which is what filesystem.xml declares. The expand step settles pending node loads and expands twice: the tree's leaf test resolves a node's type definition lazily, so on the first pass every file still drew an expand twisty. macOS render pending a Windows re-render; validation-only.

Data view (the TimeVal window, TimedDataModel) — one item's raw history as a value table (source timestamp / value / quality / server timestamp). Untagged until 2026-08-01, so the managed-image gate skipped it, and the fixture spec named no item — TimedDataModel::Init takes its series from a single Item/path — so it rendered its header row over an empty body. Now seeded with TIT.211 (Температура) and guarded by min_rows:10. Width trimmed 800 -> 560 to match the view's own fixed columns (150/150/65/150 in MakeColumns); those widths also clip the two timestamp columns and the Quality header, which is the view's sizing, not the capture's. macOS render pending a Windows re-render; validation-only.

Summary grid (the Summ window, SummaryModel over aui::Grid): one column per configured data item against a fixed time axis — hourly aggregate rows over the fixture day, four items across two devices (ЭСТРА-ПС active/reactive power, Трансформатор T1 temperature, Диагностика frequency). Untagged until 2026-08-01, so the managed-image gate skipped it and the on-disk render sat stale — and the fixture spec configured no items at all, so it showed its 16 time rows beside a blank body, an empty capture the min_rows guard cannot see (the summary's data is in its columns). The spec now carries min_columns:4, which fails the capture if the items stop reaching the grid, plus column_width:240 (at 1120 px wide) so each header renders the item's full display path instead of an elided fragment. Values are right-aligned as of 2026-08-01: the grid adapter used to hand Qt the aui alignment enum raw, so every aui::Grid rendered left-aligned no matter what its columns asked for. macOS render pending a Windows re-render; validation-only, not published to the manual (scada-docs client/summary.md embeds only menu-summary.png).

Current-events panel (the docked Event window, EventView with is_panel=true) — the unacked-only surface, as distinct from the EventJournal history in events-log.png. Renders the fixture's two pending alarms (ids 1008/1009, acknowledged:false); every other fixture event defaults to acked and is deliberately absent. Untagged until 2026-08-01, so the managed-image gate skipped it and the on-disk render sat stale from before those pending alarms existed — showing a header row over an empty body. min_rows:2 on the fixture spec now fails the capture if the unacked path stops delivering. Validation-only.

Legacy event journal (the EventJournal window, EventView with is_panel=false) in the no-theme pipeline — history over the fixture's nine events, acked and pending alike, as distinct from the unacked-only panel in events.png and the themed alarm surface in events-alarm-surface.png. Untagged until 2026-08-01, so the managed-image gate skipped it and the on-disk render sat stale; unlike events.png its content was never wrong, since the journal shows acked history the fixture has always had. Validation-only. Re-rendered 2026-08-01: the fixture now seeds four AUDIT events (AddIdentity / ModifyUser / a refused RemoveUser / a session activation), so they appear here interleaved with the process events. That is correct - the journal is every event and the Audit log view is a scoped subset of it - but it does mean an OPERATOR's journal shows administrative entries. Worth a product decision if that is unwanted; the behaviour is not new (session-activation audits were already stored), the fixture just makes it visible.

Fixture seeds two pending alarms (ids 1008/1009, acknowledged:false). KPI severity tile strip (backlog 2.3): the context bar's Critical / Warning / Unacknowledged tiles rendered by SeverityTileStrip from BuildSeverityTiles() — most severe first, severity-coloured and bold while a count is live, muted at zero; unacknowledged carries no severity colour (workflow state, not severity). Captured standalone from seeded counts (1 critical / 3 warning / 7 unacknowledged) because the fixture holds no unacknowledged alarms, so the in-window tiles would all render zero. Theme-gated reshell chrome — MakeSeverityTileStrip returns nullptr under the legacy theme; guarded by client_screenshot_check_themed.

Top context bar command/search field (shell.md §2.2): the command palette's entry point, drawn by CommandField as a read-only QLineEdit with a leading Lucide magnifier tinted from QPalette::PlaceholderText and a trailing shortcut hint in the platform's own key notation (⌘K on macOS, Ctrl+K on Windows). Captured standalone, like severity-tiles.png, because the field is chrome rather than a view; built with the same prompt and shortcut MainWindow::CreateContextBar() gives it. Everything is sized in font/style metrics, so a diff here that only changes the field's width is usually a font difference, not a UI change. Theme-gated reshell chrome — the capture is a no-op under the legacy theme; guarded by client_screenshot_check_themed.

Theme-gated reshell chrome (backlog 5.1); the legacy Users view is the generic node-table grid, so it is excluded from the no-theme managed check and guarded by client_screenshot_check_themed. Row selection drives the shared SelectionModel → the RBAC inspector. Backend/Areas/Status/Last-login from the mockup are server-side, absent from the client node model. Fixture Users folder (13 users). The manual prose for this surface is written (scada-docs client/workbench.md + en/ mirror, #administration); the image is NOT embedded yet because the published set must come from the WINDOWS pipeline - a macOS render differs by font alone and would commit as churn. Embed it on the next Windows regeneration, set published:true and add it to current_generator_owned_subset.
